description: Emphasises SPECTRAL CHANGE: amplitude gain is applied to newly prominent spectral components, window to window - onsets, note changes and any fresh spectral energy get 'plucked' out of the texture. gain 1 is a byte-identical passthrough (verified); gain 0 is legal and NOT a passthrough (it suppresses the changing components' boost path - render differs from the input). Static duration (2.0230 / 1.5209); deterministic; gain breakpoint-capable (banner-confirmed 'gain may vary over time'; a 1-to-20 ramp differs from both scalar-endpoint renders). Operates on PVOC analysis files (.ana).
musical_use: A spectral transient exciter: raise gain and every new event grows an attack halo - good for re-articulating material that spectral processing (blur, freeze, stretch) has smoothed flat, or for exaggerating note changes in legato lines into plucked/struck articulation. On steady sources it does little by design (nothing is 'newly prominent' - our sustained gliss probe barely moved at gain 20), so judge it on evolving material. The manual pairs it with spectral arpeggiation-type processes to sharpen their moving edge. A breakpoint gain lets articulation emphasis grow or fade across a phrase.

gain.description: Amplitude gain applied to newly prominent spectral components. CDP-enforced 0 to 1000 ('100000' refused verbatim: 'Parameter[1] Value (100000.000000) out of range (0.000000 to 1000.000000)'; 0 accepted). gain 1 is a verified byte-identical no-op. May vary over time via breakpoint file (verified). Required positional.

examples.description: Moderate re-articulation of a smoothed texture.
examples.expected_use: New spectral components at each event jump forward; sustained material is untouched.

examples.description: Articulation that grows across the phrase.
examples.expected_use: Starts transparent (gain 1 = verified no-op) and ends with strongly plucked onsets.

known_issues: Effect strength is entirely source-dependent: steady spectra produce little change even at high gain (verified -14.1 dBFS at gain 20 on a sustained probe) - feed it evolving material.
gain 0 is legal but NOT a passthrough (verified distinct from the input); the identity value is 1.
Large gains on busy material can push channel amps far above full scale - trim with spec gain before resynthesis.
